Atira therefore represents an uncommon low-albedo outcome, compatible with delivery of dark material from the inner Main Belt or more distant primitive populations. Further characterization of inner-Earth asteroids will test whether current population models reproduce their compositional diversity.

title: Non-Gaussian transport in tempered fractional Laplace motion
abstract: We study a minimal stochastic model for active transport featuring a non-Gaussian displacement probability density function and transient superdiffusion. Our approach is based on a combination of an exponential tempering in the parental fractional Brownian noise correlations, augmented by a gamma-distribution of the diffusivity across the ensemble. For the resulting tempered fractional Laplace motion we derive analytical expressions for the mean-squared displacement, the kurtosis, the non-Gaussianity parameter and the displacement probability density function. We also show via stochastic simulations that the model quantitatively reproduces the main experimental observations in a recent study of active cargo particle transport by a carpet of amoeba cells.

title: Apple Vision Pro: The good, the bad, the ugly
abstract: Apple Vision Pro (AVP), the headset Apple introduced as its first ``spatial computer,'' built by a single, vertically integrated vendor, entered the market in February 2024 and has since accumulated a fast-growing body of primary research spanning surgery, education, accessibility, design, and human-computer interaction. In this paper, we adopt the tripartite structure of Leone's 1966 film to organize a systematic review of this literature: we cataloged the validated, working applications of AVP (the good), the persistent technical and ergonomic limitations of a still-early-generation headset (the bad), and the ethical concerns and structural harms that follow from deliberate design, marketing, and deployment choices (the ugly). The review is built from a Scopus export of 218 records mentioning AVP, which we narrowed to 104 papers (2024--2026) with a primary focus on AVP, using explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria that we report in full, alongside a PRISMA-informed flow diagram of the screening process. We find the corpus heavily skewed toward validating benefits (medicine and surgery, education, and software tooling account for over half of the included papers) and comparatively thin on documented risks or misuse, a pattern we treat as a finding in its own right rather than a limitation to be explained away. We further show that several recurring issues, namely price, simulated social presence, and the gaze-tracking privacy architecture, resist a clean separation into ``bad'' or ``ugly'' using the published evidence alone, since both readings remain compatible with the same data. We close by identifying where the evidence base most needs to grow: independent risk and ethics research, bystander- and equity-focused study designs, and disclosure that would let researchers distinguish an engineering backlog from a structural choice.

title: Seven Years of TESS Precovery Observations of the Dwarf-planet Candidate 2026 ED$_{138}$
abstract: The trans-Neptunian object 2026 ED$_{138}$ was announced in 2026 October as the first dwarf-planet candidate in our solar system discovered by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) observed it in five month-long sectors between 2019 and 2026, four of them before its discovery. We subtract every Gaia DR3 star from these crowded full-frame images with the TESS-Gaia Light Curve (TGLC) package, then remove static residuals with a running median. Stacking the images along its predicted path detects 2026 ED$_{138}$ in all five sectors at 5-21$σ$, and at 34$σ$ combined. The TESS positions alone confirm the JPL orbit, and its brightness is consistent with the 0.08 mag fading expected from its increasing distance and changing phase angle.

title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
abstract: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.

title: On the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv Problem for $\mathbb{Z}_n^r$
abstract: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.

title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
abstract: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.

title: Multi-excited random walks on general trees
abstract: We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.

title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
abstract: Let $π_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\simλn/\log n$, it converges to $2Φ(\sqrt{λ/π})-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.

title: The coupled spread of information and potential-driven motion in evacuating agent populations
abstract: Whether a population evacuates safely depends on two coupled processes: how a warning spreads through it, and how that information moves people. We model this coupling with an agent-based framework, in which each agent's information state--susceptible, exposed, informed or reverted--gates its motion. Only informed agents respond to a global background potential encoding hazards and safe zones, while all agents interact locally through a Lennard-Jones potential. The total potential experienced by an agent drives an Ito stochastic differential equation. Tests show that landscapes with potential minima leave far fewer agents never exposed than in a flat, uniform potential control landscape, as informed agents driven toward the minima sweep past susceptible neighbors. In our tests, conduit routes raise the fraction of agents in the safe-zone minima, but leave greater numbers of agents never exposed, when compared to an unguided evacuation. This is attributed to conduits shortening trips at the cost of informed agents having fewer encounters with susceptible neighbors who could receive their information. Independently, the effective information transmission rate estimated from these encounters falls roughly sixty-fold below its well-mixed value within the first time unit, because state transitions create spatial mechanisms of net transmission suppression that mean-field closure does not capture.

title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
abstract: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.

title: Dissipative controller as a hidden source of errors in quantum gates
abstract: Quantum systems are typically controlled by classical devices that necessarily dissipate energy to the surrounding environment. By the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, this implies noise in the control field produced. We investigate the relationship between the resulting errors and the entropy produced by the macroscopic controller, working in the context of a concrete minimal model. In the most experimentally relevant regime of fast control and high fidelity, we find a tradeoff between dissipation and control errors. These findings are exemplified by perturbative calculations of the gate fidelity for simple gate implementations and of the fidelity of state transfer via shortcuts to adiabaticity in the Landau-Zener model. Our results quantitatively demonstrate that suppressing errors in quantum control typically comes at the cost of macroscopic dissipation, which is needed to tame fluctuations in the classical controller.

title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
abstract: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
abstract: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.

title: The S-function at arbitrary order: hyperplanes of symmetries and the realisability condition
abstract: For a scalar equation $y^{(n)}=\varphi(x,y,\dots,y^{(n-1)})$ the $S$-function of the extended Prelle--Singer method is a vector $S=(S_0,\dots,S_{n-2})$, the null-form vector of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Lakshmanan and collaborators, and the jet gradient of a first integral solves the adjoint of the variational equation. We describe the solutions of the system satisfied by $S$ intrinsically, and determine which of them come from first integrals. Over the field $C$ of first integrals the solutions are exactly the hyperplanes of the $n$-dimensional space $VV$ of symmetry characteristics, recovered from $n-1$ independent characteristics by a Plücker formula; in flow-box coordinates they are the hyperplane fields on the local space of leaves. A solution is the $S$-vector of a first integral if and only if the corresponding hyperplane field is integrable. This Frobenius condition splits into the $S$-system itself plus $\binom n3$ further differential conditions, so it is vacuous for $n=2$ and a genuine restriction for every $n\ge3$, for which we give an explicit non-realisable solution. The same picture explains why $λ$-symmetries and $S$-functions coincide only when $n=2$: line fields and hyperplane fields agree only on surfaces. For the computation of $S$ we record that the system is equivalent to one scalar equation for the last component, which is the Riccati form of the adjoint variational equation, and we spell out what this does and does not imply for a rational search.
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota

title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
abstract: Bérczi, Gehér, Imolay, Lovász, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,α}$, $0<α<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.

title: Counting approximate breakpoint medians of random genomes
abstract: Unsigned linear unichromosomal genomes with genes labeled 1, . . . , n are represented by permutations of these labels, whose adjacencies are the unordered pairs of genes occurring consecutively. The breakpoint distance counts the adjacencies of one genome that are absent from the other, and a breakpoint median minimizes the total breakpoint distance to a given set of genomes. Deciding whether a permutation is a median often requires a minimization over the whole symmetric group, which makes the median set resistant to exact counting. We replace this global condition by a local one: a c-approximate median is a genome having at most c adjacencies absent from all the input genomes. For a fixed genome we introduce its approximate median inverse, the set of ordered k-tuples of genomes ad- mitting it as a c-approximate median, and we construct and count this set explicitly. For k genomes chosen uniformly and independently at random, this gives the probability that a given genome is a c-approximate median and the expected number of such approximate medians. The relaxation is not only technical: approximate medians and near-optimal genomes co- incide up to a shift of the tolerance that remains bounded in probability as the number of genes grows. Finally, we derive an explicit upper bound on the probability that a given genome is an exact median, and on the expected number of exact breakpoint medians.

title: HEMO: Harness Self-Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Automatic operator design (AOD) has increasingly adopted large language models (LLMs) to generate problem-specific search and variation operators for multi-objective combinatorial optimization (MOCO). Yet most methods evolve the operators while leaving the process that discovers them fixed. This limits adaptation as new Pareto trade-offs and operator interactions change where and how the search should proceed. We introduce HEMO, which makes the AOD harness itself a self-evolving optimization target. HEMO maintains a persistent harness state and updates one module at a time, revising the logic that determines which experience to retrieve, which operators to improve, which parents to select, and how to formulate the orchestration of search steps. Downstream solution quality and runtime guide these updates, while a discounted UCB scheduler directs adaptation toward promising modules as their utility changes. A persistent memory filesystem preserves candidate outcomes and diagnostic feedback across harness states, enabling successive states to build on accumulated optimization experience. Experiments across eight MOCO tasks and two structurally distinct evolutionary backbones demonstrate strong performance against conventional evolutionary, neural, and LLM-based AOD baselines, together with effective transfer to related tasks. HEMO extends automatic operator design beyond evolving individual operators to improving the search process that discovers them.

title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

title: Identifying narrow-band mutual coupling resonances in SKA-low stations using frequency-independent current basis functions
abstract: Mutual coupling between closely spaced elements in aperture arrays introduces narrow-band spectral features in the Embedded Element Patterns (EEPs), threatening measurements of the 21-cm power spectrum with instruments such as SKA-low. We detail a method to identify such features through the construction of frequency-independent current basis functions, utilising a singular value decomposition of frequency-dependent basis functions. We demonstrate the method on a three-element linear array and full pseudo-random station of SKA log-periodic antennas and examine the current power induced by mutual coupling. For the pseudo-random layout station we note many narrow-band resonance features, including strong resonances at 50.8~MHz and 83.6~MHz, where the coupled power on the passive antennas can approach or exceed that of the excited antenna. Simulated delay power spectra for the SKA-low core show that observing in frequency bands including resonance features causes large foreground leakage within the delay power spectra, obscuring the EoR window. For the pseudo-random layout station with SKALA4.0 we identify two significant frequency bands from 59.2--76.2~MHz and 84.2--103.3~MHz which are free of contamination from current resonances, preserving the EoR window in these frequency ranges.

title: Human--AI Interactions as First-Class Data: A Formal Interaction Model and Runtime for Explainable AI Collaboration
abstract: AI assistants are increasingly embedded in computational notebooks, scientific workflows, software engineering tools, and learning systems, yet human-AI interactions are often treated as transient prompt-response exchanges rather than durable data products, hindering reproducibility, explainability, replay, behavioral analysis, and adaptive AI support. We argue that these interactions form a new data class requiring formal representation and introduce the Human-AI Interaction Description Language (HAIDL), a formal interaction model with a Backus-Naur Form-inspired concrete syntax. HAIDL encodes each interaction as a structured object capturing computational context, user request, prompt payload, AI response, feedback, problem context, provenance, and model metadata. We integrate this vision into HAIDL-X, a middleware for JupyterLab that instantiates HAIDL by capturing user-bot state, building contextualized prompts, interfacing with AI providers, collecting feedback, and storing interactions in a repository. We add a learning layer over HAIDL that maps interaction objects and notebook execution traces into reproducible measures of user behavior, including engagement, performance, help-seeking, error-oriented use, and learning personas. HAIDL-X provides a foundation for treating human-AI collaboration as structured, queryable, replayable, analyzable data.

title: Thermodynamic Crossovers in Supercritical Matter: One, No One, and One Hundred Thousand
abstract: Beyond a critical point, two thermodynamic phases become continuously connected, without being separated by any thermodynamic singularity. The paradigmatic example is the liquid-gas transition, where several criteria have been proposed to distinguish liquid-like and gas-like regimes within the supercritical region. Recently, a pair of thermodynamic crossover lines, $L^\pm$, was introduced to address a proposed incompatibility of previous definitions with the universal critical behavior of the Ising model. These lines divide the supercritical region into three regimes, meet only at the critical point, and obey the expected critical scaling laws. Here, we demonstrate that these requirements do not uniquely determine the crossover boundaries. Instead, infinitely many pairs of lines satisfy the same conditions, with different choices of thermodynamic paths selecting different crossover boundaries. We further show that the Lee-Yang formalism, despite providing an intrinsic characterization of critical singularities, does not resolve this ambiguity in defining real-axis crossover boundaries. Restricting to regular probing paths that respect the $Z_2$ symmetry of the critical point recovers the Widom and $L^\pm$ prescriptions asymptotically. This restriction, however, is a choice of protocol rather than a property of the system, and even then two inequivalent prescriptions survive. Our results demonstrate that universal critical behavior alone does not select privileged supercritical thermodynamic crossover boundaries. While such lines may identify physically meaningful changes in thermodynamic, structural, or transport properties, their precise locations and the widths of the regions they delimit remain dependent on the operational criteria used to define them.

title: Complexity of finding color-avoiding connected components
abstract: Two vertices of a (not necessarily properly) arc-colored digraph are called arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected if, after the removal of the arcs of any at most $\ell$ colors, they remain strongly $k$-arc-connected. The arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components are maximal sets of vertices such that any two of those vertices belonging to the set are arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected in the graph. We investigate the problems of finding the arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components and the maximal arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected subgraphs of an arc-colored digraph. We also consider possible generalizations to $k$-vertex-connectivity and to vertex-colored digraphs. We show that despite the seemingly minor differences in definitions, the complexity of these problems varies significantly: some can be solved in polynomial time, while others are NP-hard. It also turns out that in some cases the problem is NP-hard when multiple colors can be assigned to each vertex, but the problem becomes polynomial-time solvable when each vertex is single-colored.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Neural Networks Developed for MBHB Coalescence in the Context of LISA Space Mission
abstract: Machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly explored to analyse gravitational wave (GW) data expected from the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). At the same time, advances in quantum computing have stimulated interest in quantum machine learning as a potential alternative to conventional approaches. We investigate the applicability of quantum, hybrid quantum-classical, and classical ML models to two tasks relevant for LISA observations of massive black hole binaries: GW signal detection and merger prediction. Using the Sangria dataset from the LISA Data Challenge, we benchmark several quantum architectures, including variational quantum classifiers (VQCs), post VQC hybrid models, quantum kernel methods, data reuploading classifiers, and quantum long short-term memory (QLSTM) networks, against classical support vector machines, multilayer perceptrons, recurrent neural networks, and LSTM networks. The models are trained on labelled data derived from the Sangria training dataset and evaluated on the corresponding blind dataset. For signal detection, several quantum models match or outperform classical baselines. In particular, the best performing hybrid post VQC architecture correctly identifies all signal samples in the blind dataset, while the standard VQC and data reuploading classifier achieve competitive detection rates. For merger detection and coalescence time estimation, however, the standard VQC emerges as the most reliable model, successfully localising all detected merger events with the lowest localisation errors. We further analyse the trade-offs between predictive performance, model complexity, and quantum circuit resources. Our results indicate that, although no universal quantum advantage is observed, selected quantum models can provide practical benefits for specific GW analysis tasks and represent promising candidates for future LISA data analysis pipelines.

title: Nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to quantum reservoirs
abstract: A statistical mechanical formulation where nonequilibrium averages of selected quantum observables are given exactly as averages over local density operators is used to describe the dynamics and thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to reservoirs. The local density operators are functionals of constraint variables that play the role of thermodynamic forces that satisfy a set of equations of motion. A focus of the work is on the evolution of the average internal energy of the quantum subsystem that may be subject to external autonomous driving that does work on the system, and on entropy production in the system. The nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics the quantum subsystem coupled to reservoirs, as well as that for the isolated subsystem and reservoirs, are discussed. When the subsystem is coupled to large quantum reservoirs, the effects of the quantum subsystem on the reservoirs can be captured through boundary conditions on the reservoir equations, and these boundary conditions are derived. The formulation is illustrated by considering the heat transfer through a system comprising a quantum system coupled to two heat reservoirs with different temperatures.

title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
abstract: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.

title: Dense Minors from the Crux
abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_α(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $αd$ for any fixed $0<α<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $Ω(\sqrt{d\,C_α(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

title: Mind The Gap (MTG-AD): Dataset and Fine-grained Evaluation for End-to-End Inline Audio Descriptions
abstract: Audio descriptions (AD) are essential for making visual media accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) users. While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a scalable solution for generating audio descriptions on-demand, their performance on ``inline'' audio descriptions -- which must fit within existing silences in a video -- remains under-explored, particularly for diverse user-generated content (UGC). We present a comprehensive investigation into MLLM-generated inline audio descriptions. First, we introduce MTG-AD, a professionally annotated dataset of 36 hours of videos, each averaging $\sim$5 mins. and 8k+ descriptions in total, co-created by paired blind and sighted AD professionals to provide a high-quality benchmark for this task. Second, we propose MTG-AD-Eval, an evaluation framework based on audio description expert guidelines that provides fine-grained, reference-free actionable metrics for model improvement. Crucially, our framework evaluates the end-to-end task: it renders the generated scripts into audio tracks to assess their fit within the original video's natural silences, minimizing disruptive overlaps. Our analysis across frontier MLLMs reveals that while models accurately describe visual events and substantially reduce speech overlaps, gaps persist in narrative pacing and flow. Finally, we empirically validate that our automated and reference-free metrics correlate significantly with human quality ratings from sighted raters and 7 BLV participants, finding that while users narrowly prefer human-authored audio descriptions, they find MLLM-generated audio descriptions highly beneficial for comprehension. We provide actionable system design guidance and release MTG-AD at https://hf.co/datasets/google/mind-the-gap-inline-ad and MTG-AD-Eval at https://github.com/google/mtg-ad.

title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
abstract: A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.

title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
abstract: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $α$-$μ$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

title: Monte Carlo simulation of mixed spin-orbit ordering
abstract: The effect of a magnetic field on the thermodynamic properties of the Kugel-Khomskii model with maximal entanglement using the quasi-classical Monte Carlo method with the heat bath algorithm. The temperature dependencies of single-site correlators show that the application of a magnetic field results in non-zero magnetization and the simultaneous appearance of an orbital ordering at the same point in the Brillouin zone where a non-zero spin-orbit correlator exists.

title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
abstract: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.

title: Ensemble-dependent effect of disorder on multicritical points in a system with long-range interactions
abstract: We introduce two variants of the Blume--Emery--Griffiths model with long-range, mean-field-like interactions and quenched disorder. Although the two variants are described by different Hamiltonians, they yield the same free energy. Moreover, both Hamiltonians lead to the same average energy and hence to the same microcanonical entropy. The canonical and microcanonical phase boundaries differ markedly, and so does the multicritical behaviour of the two ensembles. In the microcanonical ensemble, tricritical points appear for any fraction of active spins, whereas in the canonical ensemble they emerge only when this fraction is sufficiently large. At lower fractions, canonical critical endpoints arise instead. We also report the formation of gaps in the entropy as a function of magnetization, another manifestation of ensemble inequivalence.

title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
abstract: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $μ$, a $μ$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

title: Learning Calibrated Confidence for Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract: Complex information seeking on the Web often requires collecting evidence from multiple documents and reasoning across them, as in multi-hop question answering. Multi-agent systems address such tasks by dividing work among specialized agents, where upstream agents produce intermediate answers and supporting evidence that downstream agents build upon. However, upstream answers vary in correctness, and most systems provide no quantitative signal about it, leaving the downstream agent to judge whether to trust or verify what it receives based solely on the textual evidence. In this paper, we propose MASCAL. Each agent learns to produce a correctness probability for its answer by jointly optimizing task performance and confidence calibration in reinforcement learning; the upstream agent passes this probability at handoff, giving the downstream agent a quantitative basis for its decisions, and the final answer also carries a calibrated probability, quantifying the reliability of the system output. To guide the downstream agent in using this signal during training, we introduce confidence-aware weighting, which increases the learning weight at positions responsive to the upstream probability, so that the agent learns more from decisions where it actively uses the signal. Across three collaboration architectures spanning Web retrieval and reasoning tasks, MASCAL improves task accuracy and calibration quality for both agents, and generalizes to deeper collaboration chains and different model scales. Intervention analysis confirms that upstream confidence affects downstream decision behavior, and the learned final confidence supports selective answering and targeted rechecking.

title: Preparation of a celestial field for precise VLBI observations of the JUICE spacecraft: a test case of the Venus flyby
abstract: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer mission, launched in 2023, is on its way to the Jovian system, to arrive in 2031. The Planetary Radio Interferometry and Doppler Experiment performs radio astronomical observations of the spacecraft already in its interplanetary cruise phase. Since the sky density of potential compact radio sources suitable as phase-reference calibrators in very long baseline interferometry observations is low, densifying the celestial reference frame along the Ecliptic is an essential task in support of JUICE. In preparation for the JUICE gravity assist manoeuvre at Venus in August 2025, to support the accurate reconstruction of the spacecraft state vector, we selected in-beam calibrator source candidates along the JUICE trajectory. Additionally, we attempted to link known nearby bright compact reference sources from the Radio Fundamental Catalog to the International Celestial Reference Frame. We performed nodding-style phase-referencing VLBI observations with the European VLBI Network at 8.4GHz, targeting nine in-beam calibrator candidate and three RFC sources in the celestial vicinity of JUICE's trajectory during its Venus flyby. We linked their positions to nearby ICRF sources by means of relative astrometry. Four of the ICC targets and all RFC sources were detected and imaged with the EVN, and their coordinates determined with typically sub-mas precision. Although none of the targeted ICC sources proved suitable as VLBI phase-reference calibrators because of being too faint or resolved, their newly-determined positions and flux densities could in principle be used to verify the detection of the spacecraft at the time of the actual flyby around Venus. During the detailed analysis of the ICC targets, we found that the structure of one of them, J0843+1826 is resolved on mas scale, and the other one, J0843+1814 is a young radio galaxy, likely a member of a cluster.

title: Lie point symmetry analysis of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model with exponential claim sizes
abstract: We carry out a Lie point symmetry analysis of the coupled integro-differential system satisfied by the conditional Gerber--Shiu functions of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model. In the model, claim sizes are exponential, the intensity of the next claim arrival depends on whether the current claim exceeds a random threshold, and both the volatility and the premium rate may depend on the surplus. We write the system as the restriction to the half-line of a far-field operator with prescribed exterior data, derive the complete set of determining equations, including the condition imposed by the nonlocal convolution term, and solve them. The resulting group classification holds for every surplus-dependent volatility and premium of the form considered and for every absolutely continuous or constant threshold distribution. A non-trivial symmetry beyond scaling and superposition exists if and only if the volatility and the premium rate are constant, and it is then exactly the translation in the surplus variable. We construct the optimal system of one-dimensional subalgebras. We show that the invariant solutions of the combined translation--scaling generators exist precisely when a $2\times2$ generalized Lundberg determinant vanishes, and we give this determinant for an arbitrary threshold distribution, with explicit forms for the constant and exponential thresholds. We prove existence and sign properties of the adjustment coefficient, derive its sensitivities to all model parameters, and establish Cramér--Lundberg-type asymptotics for the Gerber--Shiu functions, including the limit of the ratio between the two regimes. A numerical study shows that claim-size-driven dependence lowers the adjustment coefficient markedly below that of an independent model with the same mean claim intensity.

title: Sequince: a modular sequential Monte Carlo toolkit
abstract: Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods approximate sequences of probability distributions using populations of weighted samples and are widely applicable, including in Bayesian inference and particle filtering. We present sequince, a modular Python toolkit for constructing SMC algorithms from reusable and extensible components. The toolkit provides modular steps for weighting, resampling, mutation, transformation, and control operations that are composed to implement different algorithms. It also includes prebuilt samplers for tempered SMC, persistent sampling and nested sampling via SMC. Its core components follow the Python Array API standard, supporting NumPy, JAX, PyTorch, and CuPy, enabling analyses on CPUs or GPUs. Random-number control and checkpointing support reproducible scientific workflows. This paper describes sequince v0.1.0 and its design as reusable infrastructure for methodological research and application of SMC methods.

title: The Verification Wall in Microbial Metabolomics
abstract: Computational methods now propose structures for gut microbial metabolites faster than any laboratory can confirm them. We argue that verification, not generation, is the binding constraint, and that better models will not relieve it. Confirming a structure to the field's own standard means having the molecule in hand. Automation can lower what that costs per compound, but the cost stays proportional to the number of structures and never amortizes across them. Two substitutes are on offer and neither removes that requirement. In-silico spectral prediction ranks candidates instead of confirming one, and the strongest current model puts the right structure first 33.5% of the time on a scaffold-split benchmark. Any assignment resting on spectral similarity is, by the field's own definition, made without a reference standard. Microcrystal diffraction does return a structure, but it needs the compound to crystallize out of a trace mixture, which is a different problem rather than an easier one. We sorted 10,645 computationally inferred metabolite structures by what verifying each would take. Between 5% and 37% have no verification route identified under our analysis. That spread reflects where the thresholds are set rather than a measured count of unverifiable compounds, and the inaccessible ones cluster among the most speculative entries. Those figures understate the problem, because the gut makes far more compounds than any database records. HMDB holds only what someone has already thought worth cataloguing, and structure generators are bounded by nothing at all. The claim is easy to disprove. Show a route that confirms structures as fast as they are proposed. Until someone does, two problems stay unsolved. Nobody knows how to spend a verification budget that will always be too small, or what a biologist may conclude from a structure that was never confirmed.

title: From if to Oops: Turning a conditional into a key-recovery oracle
abstract: Deterministic variants of CSIDH remove randomness from the group action, either through implementation techniques or, as in Houben's deterministic CSIDH and OSIDH-LD, by design. Since earlier fault attacks on CSIDH mostly target random point sampling, determinism seems to close that avenue. We show that it opens another: every secret-dependent step occurs at a fixed, public point of every execution, so an attacker can fault the same step repeatedly. Our attack forces the mask that selects which of two lanes computes the next isogeny to zero, for example by skipping one instruction. Whether the output changes reveals whether a secret exponent reaches a chosen threshold, and a binary search over these thresholds recovers the full key with one fault per execution: at most 297 oracle queries for OSIDH-LD and 222 for deterministic CSIDH with CSIDH-512-sized keys. We recover full OSIDH-LD keys in a software fault simulation of the reference implementation, and show on a ChipWhisperer-Lite that the targeted instruction is skipped with probability at least 0.94 at an isolated fault position. Finally, we argue that fault resistance requires giving up determinism, and propose countermeasures relying on randomization.

title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
abstract: Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines a geometric construction in characteristic two with an incidence matrix factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The same construction yields integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $Ω_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

title: Structural Change in the Multilayer World Trade Web: An Economic Dominance Theory Approach
abstract: Most studies of the World Trade Web (WTW) describe its topology: degrees, strengths, centralities, communities, or the similarity between product networks and years. This paper presents Economic Dominance Theory (EDT), initiated by Lantner (1974), and positions it as an alternative theory of structural dependence in directed flow networks rather than an additional toolbox. EDT normalizes bilateral flows into a Ghosh matrix of directed propagation and measures circular interdependence through its determinant, which aggregates the feedback circuits by which influence returns to its origin. Through the log-determinant and its trace expansion, a single quantity decomposes exactly by feedback length, arc and node deletion, product layer, network partition and, in the dynamic extension developed here, time. Structural change can therefore be measured without defining a distance between graphs, and layers and regions become exact components of one object rather than separate descriptions. EDT differs from centrality and community detection, which describe positions and densities rather than feedback closure; from economic complexity, which addresses capabilities rather than dependence; and from input-output and value-chain analysis, whose algebra it shares but which locate positions along chains where EDT measures their closure. An application to CEPII BACI data (1995-2023, 96 HS2 layers) shows what this adds. Circular interdependence did not deepen with trade: the diffusion determinant, which rises when feedback weakens, goes from 0.12 in 1995 to 0.21 in 2006, falls to 0.16 in 2013 and reaches 0.19 in 2023. This net weakening comes from cross-product feedback, which carries more than 90% of order-two and about 99% of order-three feedback. Geography depends on feedback length: short reciprocal loops remain regional, while long feedback is overwhelmingly transregional.

title: Inkitiate: Initiating and Steering Agent Assistance through Ink in a Spatial Workspace
abstract: Handwriting and sketching help people develop ideas around information. As this work unfolds, users may seek assistance with finding, understanding, and organizing materials. We investigate how ink can initiate and steer agent assistance in this process. An eight-participant formative study explored desired assistance and interaction expectations, informing three connected activities: bringing materials in, thinking with materials, and shaping the space. We present Inkitiate, a spatial workspace for ink-based agent assistance in knowledge work. Through ink, users retrieve external materials, build on accumulated content and results, and reorganize the canvas, while inspecting and guiding agent actions. In a study with eighteen participants, users reported favorable usability and low perceived workload, and used retained ink and materials to develop further ink queries. An ink-query vocabulary and cases reveal how users combine linguistic and graphical expressions to direct agents. These findings inform ink-based agent interaction design for expressive requests and continued work with materials.

title: Interacting particles in random irregular media
abstract: In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.

title: The asymptotic number of zonotopes
abstract: We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{á}r{á}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our analysis is based on a correspondence between power sums over primitive vectors (vectors with coprime coordinates) and Eulerian polynomials. We also analyse some combinatorial properties of lattice zonotopes. In particular, we compute the asymptotic mean and variance of the diameter of the graph of a random lattice zonotope inscribed in [0, n] d as n goes to infinity, and show that this diameter satisfies a central limit theorem.

title: ExploreRepair: Evidence-Specialized Agents for Vulnerability Repair under Information Constraints
abstract: Automated vulnerability repair must often operate with incomplete vulnerability information: developers may lack an accurate vulnerability classification or a provided proof-of-vulnerability (PoV) test, yet still need to produce a repair. Without detailed information, a key challenge is to explore multiple plausible interpretations of the vulnerability before committing to a repair. To address this challenge, we propose ExploreRepair, a vulnerability repair framework that reconciles the vulnerability observations and repair implementations from a team of exploration agents. We first collect these observations and repair implementations from three agents, each tasked with exploring a specific dimension of the vulnerability. Then, a Lesson Aggregator and a Patch Aggregator independently synthesize repairs from these observations and concrete implementations before a final Aggregator reconciles their proposals without benchmark feedback. On PatchEval, ExploreRepair achieves repair success rates of 39.6% and 71.6% with GPT-5.6-Luna and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, respectively, exceeding EvoRepair, a state-of-the-art vulnerability repair approach, by 16.0 and 25.4 percentage points. On VulnLoc+, it achieves success rates of 51.4% and 62.9%, respectively, exceeding LoopRepair's variant without PoV tests by 20.0 and 17.1 percentage points.

title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
abstract: For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=σ(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{θα,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-α}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$θ$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $σ(x)\equiv x^{1+γ}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $γ\in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $γ=\frac{1}{2}$).

title: Compressed Orientation Reachability Maps for Sub-Second Robotic Needle Entry Point Planning
abstract: In the context of multi-stage trajectory planning for robotic percutaneous liver interventions, identifying a kinematically feasible entry point remains a critical computational bottleneck. Existing methods rely on exhaustive inverse kinematics or randomized searches, incurring delays of 13 to 27 seconds per target and limiting real-time intraoperative adaptation. This paper introduces an Orientation-Based Reachability Map (ORM) that precomputes the kinematic feasibility of a 6 Degrees of Freedom (DoF) serial manipulator across 188,873 workspace positions and encodes orientation feasibility into a compact, indexed 83 MB map. A Just-In-Time (JIT) compiled runtime pipeline replaces live optimization with near-instantaneous array lookups. Experimental evaluation demonstrates a reduction in planning latency from 13.5-26.9 s to 0.289-0.349 s per target while maintaining high geometric fidelity, achieving a mean convex hull volume overlap ratio of 0.933 and a mean alpha-shape volume ratio of 0.976 relative to the baseline reachable point cloud. The proposed ORM framework enables sub-second entry point planning and provides an efficient computational framework for robotic needle insertion in percutaneous liver ablation.

title: Syndrome Trellis Decryption in Post-Quantum Cryptography
abstract: We present a novel post-quantum cryptographic framework based on masked high-memory convolutional codes in the Niederreiter paradigm. The public key is derived from a high-memory polynomial parity-check matrix augmented by dense random masking and additional invertible linear transformations. The resulting matrix exhibits strong random-like properties, effectively concealing its algebraic structure and resisting known structural and algebraic attacks. Legitimate recipients retain polynomial-time decoding capability, whereas adversaries appear to be limited to generic information-set decoding with exponential complexity. Under standard cryptanalytic estimates, the proposed construction achieves security margins exceeding those of classical McEliece- and Niederreiter-based systems by factors greater than 2^200. Beyond its enhanced security profile, the construction offers considerable design flexibility, supporting arbitrary plaintext lengths, linear-time decryption, and a uniform per-bit computational cost, enabling efficient scalability to very long messages. Practical implementation is facilitated by a parallel array of syndrome-trellis decoders, dynamically instantiated according to candidate syndrome values, enabling efficient hardware and software implementations with high throughput. Overall, the proposed scheme is a promising candidate for robust, scalable, quantum-resistant public-key cryptography.

title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
abstract: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.

title: Incorporating Machine-Others: An Enactive Exploration of Human-LLM Interactions
abstract: New concepts based in interactional thinking are required to understand how humans are changed by relating to LLMs. Standard theories of technological impact upon users' autonomy are inadequate here, because this technology is capable of inducing linguistic interactions with humans in an unprecedented manner. Traditional theories of social cognition also fall short, because LLMs have neither autonomy nor minds nor sociality as such. And yet, humans interact, talk, and create with them. We base ourselves on enactive theory, particularly on the theory of Linguistic Bodies and recent developments of enactive accounts of AI, to explore how we make sense with machines. We argue that we incorporate machine-others in two ways: in the tool-like sense of incorporation as enabling particular skills, but also in the more linguistic and identity-tied sense of incorporating (and incarnating) LLMs' ways of languaging. However, LLMs are themselves excorporated and excarnated phantoms of our own languaging; we give a (machinic) body to our language. As such, we are not just incorporating machinic others; we are incorporating excorporated others. These conceptual advances draw a new map of our linguistic relation to LLMs, putting them in continuation with other forms of languaging involving other linguistic artifacts (e.g., religious books). We attend to some particular forms that this relation takes today, and how they may be impacting the autonomy and becoming of LLM-engaged humans. We introduce the idea of "susceptive sense-making" to characterize increased semiotic labour that is carried by the lack of friction that we sometimes encounter within these services.

title: From Trees to Binary Trees: Approximation Algorithms and a PTAS
abstract: Kellerhals, Krebs, Nichterlein, and Schmid introduced the optimization problem Tree in Binary Tree (TBT), where, given a tree $T$, the task is to find a binary tree $S^*$ with $V(T)=V(S^*)$ that minimizes $\sum_{uv\in E(T)} \operatorname{dist}_{S^*}(u,v)$. They also introduced the variant Tree in Binary Tree With Steiner Nodes (TBT-SN), where the condition $V(T)=V(S^*)$ is relaxed to $V(T)\subseteq V(S^*)$. We give a simple linear-time $\frac{8}{3}$-approximation algorithm for TBT and a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for TBT-SN. Our main building idea in both algorithms is to iteratively consider subtrees of the tree $T$ which contain all vertices below some vertex $v$ and construct a solution where $v$ has degree 1. For the PTAS, we cut $T$ into smaller trees, solve these instances, modify the obtained solutions, and combine them to achieve a solution for the original instance.

title: Integrating Perception, Comprehension, and Projection for Alert Validation: A Unified Cyber Situational Awareness Framework
abstract: Security Operation Centres (SOCs) must validate large volumes of alerts with limited analyst resources, yet alerts often lack sufficient context to determine whether suspicious activity is attack related. While provenance-based intrusion detection research has progressed from perception-level signals to comprehension- and projection-level cyber situational awareness (CSA), it remains unclear whether richer CSA consistently improves alert validation. This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of perception-, comprehension-,and projection-level CSA within a unified alert validation framework. Using Captain and Kairos, we generate multi-level CSA and formulate alert validation as a positive-unlabelled multi-instance learning (PU-MIL) task over CSA-derived behavioural hypotheses. Experimental evaluation on the DARPA TC dataset shows that comprehension-level CSA substantially improves validation by incorporating causal attack context. Relative to the Queue and Max. CSG baselines, PU-MIL achieves up to 28.6 and 75 percentage-point gains in Recall@5, and 24.6% and 86.8% reductions in mean positive rank on Cadets and Theia, respectively. Projection-level CSA can yield additional benefits, reducing the mean positive rank on Theia from 22.0 to 8.5 at a 40-minute projection horizon, although its effectiveness varies across projection horizons. Overall, richer CSA does not necessarily lead to better alert validation. Rather, its value depends on when and how it is introduced, motivating adaptive CSA progression that selectively enriches alerts according to validation requirements.

title: Surprise Alone Learns Lies: Evidence-Gated Continual Learning for LLMs from Streaming Claims
abstract: Continual learning methods for large language models increasingly decide what to learn by surprise, keeping the inputs the model finds least predictable. This rule is unsafe when the stream contains lies. A planted falsehood about something the model knows has low probability under the model's belief, so it is highly surprising by construction, and a surprise-driven learner absorbs nearly every such lie, at a rate similar to random selection with the same budget. We study the problem with LoRA-adapted students (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B) that learn from a stream of true and false claims about invented people and real CounterFact facts. We report four findings. (1) A verifier key, a judge that must approve each claim, removes lies to the extent that its verifier is accurate; real LLM judges are cautious and reject unsourced truths and even source-backed updates. (2) Calibrated regression tests on unrelated knowledge slow learning down without filtering out lies. (3) The original model's own prior flags claims that contradict what it knows, without a judge. It separates lies about known facts from true new facts (AUC 0.78-0.83 across three models) but not from legitimate updates of the same kind of fact (AUC 0.53). It saves 43% of judge calls, but an attacker with access to the model can choose lies that pass it. (4) If trusted sources exist that an attacker cannot plant, routing contradicted claims to evidence recovers legitimate updates and the combined system has the lowest poison rate among learned claims; when an attacker plants matching sources for 30% of the lies, the system ends up worse than the judge alone. The acceptance signals answer different questions, and none of them decides on its own whether a claim is true.

title: Exact Avoid-or-Compress Extrema for Dense Reachable Images: Defects Four and Five
abstract: Let $S$ be a reachable image of a strongly connected synchronizing automaton and $\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq S$. We determine the maximum shortest avoid-or-compress length over binary and arbitrary finite alphabets for $m=n-|S|=4$ and $m=5$. The exact values are $\min(n-|A|,11)$ and $\min(n-|A|,14)$, respectively. Uniform binary constructions attain both bounds. For the upper bounds, short-pair graphs and actual-image constraints reduce all parameters to finite necessary domains. Exhaustive checks exclude the domains, apart from a single relaxation eliminated by a multipartite overlap lemma. The largest calculation covers 3,206,988 domains.

title: High-temperature expansion of the inverse-square Ising chain in a magnetic field: exact coefficients and finite-size reconstruction
abstract: The one-dimensional Ising chain with inverse-square interactions is a paradigmatic long-range system: it exhibits the unusual Thouless transition, with a discontinuity in the spontaneous magnetization, yet its full field-dependent thermodynamics remains unknown in closed form. We develop the high-temperature expansion of its free energy while retaining the dependence on a uniform magnetic field at every order. We prove that, after a natural rescaling of the coupling, each coefficient is a rational polynomial in the squared hyperbolic tangent of the reduced field. Remarkably, at each order $n$ the field-dependent free-energy coefficient of a finite, periodically repeated ring is an exact polynomial of degree at most $n$ in $L^{-2}$. The infinite-chain coefficient is its constant term and can therefore be reconstructed from $n+1$ finite rings without numerical extrapolation. Using this reconstruction, we determine the full field-dependent expansion through order 26: 26 polynomials containing 377 rational coefficient entries. We further derive exact formulas, valid at every order, for the coefficients of the two highest powers of the field variable using matching determinants and a cycle-Laplacian reduction. These results reveal an unexpected algebraic structure in the microscopic thermodynamics of the inverse-square chain and provide high-order information about its magnetic response.

title: Critical-level wave absorption controls chaos in a wave--mean flow system
abstract: Wave-mean flow interactions in stratified fluids can drive spontaneous oscillations, yet the mechanisms controlling transitions between periodic and chaotic regimes remain poorly understood. Using a minimal one-dimensional model of wave-driven mean-flow reversals motivated by the quasi-biennial oscillation (QBO), we identify two distinct mechanisms that suppress the formation of multiple extrema in the velocity profile: critical-level momentum deposition by a broad spectrum of undamped small-scale gravity waves, and wave-amplitude growth due to exponential density stratification. Although physically distinct, both mechanisms inhibit the route to chaos and reduce sensitivity to small-scale viscosity, substantially widening the region of periodic behavior in parameter space. These results identify a general internal mechanism for the stabilization of wave-driven oscillations, with direct implications for QBO-like phenomena in geophysical and astrophysical flows.

title: InferD: A Honeypot Framework for AI Inference Infrastructure
abstract: Large language model serving stacks, commercial inference APIs, vector databases, and agent orchestration gateways are now ex- posed on the public internet and indexed by commodity scanners within hours of deployment. The threat characteristics of this sur- face are only beginning to be measured, and the honeypot frame- works that could measure it were designed for conventional net- work services rather than for AI infrastructure. In fact, emulating an AI service is a distinct deception problem: the observable behavior of the service, including model inventories, token formats, tool-call protocols, and authorization flows, must be reproduced faithfully, while the underlying computation, model inference and tool ex- ecution, must never occur. We present InferD, a low-interaction honeypot framework organized around a single principle we call deception without inference: every request an adversary can observe is answered from static response pools, and nothing an adversary submits is ever executed. InferD decomposes the emulation into four deception planes, transport, service protocol, vulnerability surface, and agentic session, adds a provenance plane that links a planted credential to evidence of downstream model-mediated processing.

title: AI at a Turning Point: From ChatGPT through Neural Networks to Neuromorphic AI
abstract: The tension between the established technologies of connectionist AI and their neuromorphic challengers is attracting growing attention, above all because of the enormous energy demand of the former and the low power consumption of the latter. Developing and running large AI models consumes gigawatt- to terawatt-hours of energy, while the human brain operates on a continuous 20 watts. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) counter this energy demand with a frugal approach and bring elements of self-organization into the methodological repertoire of AI: local learning instead of global error backpropagation, event-driven computing, and time as a carrier of information. They do not replace today's AI but extend it; in hybrid systems each approach can be deployed where its strengths lie. This monograph explains the field in a generally accessible yet mathematically rigorous way. Using the text-generation module of ChatGPT as an example, the principle, elegance, and computational cost of transformer-based AI are presented and compared with the coding, learning, and network-design methods of SNNs. Throughout, relevant mechanisms of the human nervous system serve as model and reference point. Topics include spike-timing-dependent plasticity, population and temporal coding, the Neural Engineering Framework, neuromorphic hardware from Loihi 2 to commercial edge processors, and the prospects for classical and neuromorphic AI to complement and extend each other.

title: Two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures with ECMC
abstract: We discuss reversible and non-reversible local Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures. We illustrate how the factorized Metropolis filter efficiently handles long-range interactions even for binary mixtures, using an adapted cell-veto strategy. We then benchmark the non-reversible event-chain Monte Carlo (ECMC) algorithm against the factorized Metropolis algorithm. For simple test cases, we demonstrate speedups of several orders of magnitude in the equilibrium and the out-of-equilibrium dynamics. Using the ECMC algorithm, we provide an overview of the physics of binary Lennard-Jones mixtures, from the case without depletion (no interaction between solute and solvent) all the way to the depletion limit (with a diverging number of solvent particles). We analyze the algorithms in different thermodynamic phases and in the corresponding limits.

title: Long-Term Agent Memory through Complementary Curation and Consolidation
abstract: Long-horizon dialogue agents require effective memory systems to recall facts, events, and relationships from interaction histories. In this work, we propose a hybrid-memory architecture comprising episodic memories and structured relational memories and a consolidation mechanism which preserves efficiency. We conduct an empirical study across two benchmarks: LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S. Our experiments demonstrate that the two memory types are consistently complementary, combining both outperform state-of-the-art memory frameworks and achieves 90.2% accuracy on LoCoMo and 85.5% on LongMemEval-S.

title: Robust statistical significance for Gravitational Wave inference
abstract: The field of gravitational-wave data analysis heavily relies on Bayes factors to make statements about astrophysical effects in events detected by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration. This is true on an event level, for example when discussing the potential detection of precession or eccentricity, as well as on a population level. For the latter, perhaps the main limiting factor is the reliance on the output from event-level nested sampling analyses, which is known to introduce growing uncertainties and biases as the number of detections increases. In both cases, while Bayes factors are useful when comparing different models, because the underlying distribution of Bayes factors in noise is unknown, it is often not possible to use them to make quantifiable statistical statements. Their statistical meaning is also questionable in the at least $20\%$ of gravitational-wave events that contain transient noise artifacts. This paper shows that it is possible to use evidence networks, which can infer Bayes factors after learning the distinguishability between datasets, to solve all of the aforementioned problems. By being able to calculate up to $10^5$ Bayes factors per second, we can construct background distributions of Bayes factors under different signal assumptions to estimate significance. We show that the high precision achieved allows us to scale the results from up to $10^4$ events with no discernable bias on population-level quantities, while laying the foundations for a likelihood-free method that does not rely on the assumption of Gaussian and stationary noise.

title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.

title: Assessing AI Companion Chatbot Safety for Vulnerable Users: A Crisis-Stage Multi-Platform Evaluation
abstract: AI companion chatbots are increasingly used by vulnerable individuals, including adolescents in suicidal crisis, for emotional support. Existing safety evaluations focus on base models, leaving gaps in product-level assessment, crisis-stage sensitivity, and comparisons between companion apps and general-purpose LLMs. We introduce MIRROR-Eval (Multi-turn Interaction Risk Review: Observing suicidal-crisis Responses), a dataset of 960 annotated 20-turn conversations across eight deployed platform configurations, six clinically grounded personas, and two crisis stages: ideation and explicit planning. An LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline applies an expert-reviewed rubric covering user risk severity, chatbot risk awareness, and intervention behavior. We observe a three-tier harm structure: companion apps (Character.AI and Replika) and Grok 4.3 form a high-harm tier; Gemini 3.1 Pro is mid-range; GPT-5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5 show substantially lower harm. At planning, companion apps show increased glorification and normalisation, advancement toward harmful action, and harmful methods and instructions. Crisis recognition and empathetic language do not ensure safe responses. These findings highlight the need for product-level safety evaluation across crisis stages. Dataset and code: https://huggingface.co/datasets/imda-biztech/MIRROR-Eval. Warning: this paper includes examples that may be offensive or harmful.

title: Finding Is Not Returning, Returning Is Not Reconstructing: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Agent Social Re-entry
abstract: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in persistent social environments, understanding their long-term social interaction capabilities becomes increasingly important. While existing research has advanced long-term memory and conversational context retrieval, less attention has been paid to whether agents can autonomously re-engage with previously inactive conversations. In particular, remembering a past interaction does not necessarily mean that an agent can identify when to revisit it, decide to return, or reconstruct the context needed for a coherent continuation. To investigate this gap, we introduce agent social re-entry as a multi- dimensional evaluation problem, distinguishing three complementary capabilities: Finding, Returning, and Reconstructing. We develop a shared-snapshot evaluation framework that measures these dimensions independently, allowing us to examine how conversational resurfacing and persistent memory relate to different aspects of social re-entry. Evaluations across six LLM configurations show that resurfacing substantially improves target conversation identification, while persistent memory is associated with higher rates of autonomous target-directed replying. However, neither improvement is accompanied by consistent gains in contextual reconstruction. These results highlight the distinction between accessing previous conversations, choosing to re-engage, and maintaining conversational continuity. Our framework provides a way to evaluate these capabilities separately rather than relying on memory retrieval or conversational response quality alone.
